title: Pseudo-abelian group varieties over an algebraically closed field are proper
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed and normal subgroup schemes as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-pc-scheme]. Let $Q$ be a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-group scheme. Assume that every smooth connected affine closed normal subgroup scheme $S\hookrightarrow Q$ is trivial, meaning that its identity morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$ is an isomorphism. Then $Q$ is proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. No commutativity assumption is imposed on $Q$.

source.place: Definition 8.3, printed p.149, and Theorem 8.26 with its proof, printed p.154, specialized to an algebraically closed field. Complete means proper in this finite-type separated setting. No Stacks tag states the pseudo-abelian properness theorem.

proof.text: Prove the assertion simultaneously for all such $k$-groups by strong induction on $d=\dim G$. The dimension clause of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-subgroup-products] makes $d$ a finite nonnegative integer. Apply [lem-sfb-general-group-centre-zero-dimension-affine] to form $Z=Z(G)$ and $A=(Z^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$, with $\dim A=\dim Z$. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], applied to $Z$, $A$ is a smooth connected separated finite-type group. Its inclusion in $G$ is closed: compose the closed inclusions $A\hookrightarrow Z^0\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow G$ (locally the composite of two quotient ring maps is a quotient). It is central by the defining property of $Z$.

source.place: Theorem 8.26, p.154, induction on dimension; Proposition 1.92, pp.33--34; Corollary 1.39, p.18.

proof.text: If $\dim A=0$, then $\dim Z=0$, so [lem-sfb-general-group-centre-zero-dimension-affine] makes $G$ affine. The identity inclusion $G\hookrightarrow G$ is a smooth connected affine closed normal subgroup, hence the hypothesis says that $e_G:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the structure morphism, which is finite (on affine coordinates an isomorphism is finite). It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. This case includes $d=0$, since the dimension clause in step 1 bounds $\dim A$ by $d$.

source.place: Theorem 8.26, p.154, zero-dimensional-centre case. The pseudo-abelian hypothesis directly makes an affine G trivial; no anti-affineness assumption is needed.

proof.text: Now $\dim A>0$. If $A$ were not proper, [lem-sfb-rosenlicht-nonproper-affine-subgroup] applied to $A$ would give a smooth connected affine closed subgroup $U\hookrightarrow A$ with $\dim U>0$. Its composite inclusion in $G$ is closed (compose quotient maps locally) and normal: after every algebra extension, all its elements commute with all elements of $G$, since $A$ is central. Thus the hypothesis makes $U$ trivial. But $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has dimension zero: it has a single point, hence no strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets. This contradicts $\dim U>0$. Consequently $A$ is proper, and is an abelian variety by [def-sc-abelian-variety].

source.place: Theorem 8.26, p.154, noncomplete-central-component case; Proposition 8.25, pp.153--154.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rosenlicht-connected-almost-complement] to the central abelian subvariety $A\hookrightarrow G$. Obtain a smooth connected closed normal subgroup $N$ and a faithfully flat finite-presentation homomorphism $m:A\times_kN\to G$, with finite kernel and $\dim N=\dim G-\dim A<d$. In particular $N$ has the smoothness, connectedness, separatedness and finite-type hypotheses needed for induction. For separatedness one can restrict the closed diagonal of $G$ to $N\times N$; finite type also follows from the stated finite-type group convention in the cited lemma.

source.place: Theorem 8.26, p.154, complete-central-component case; Theorem 8.24, p.153.

proof.text: Check the remaining induction hypothesis for $N$. Let $S\hookrightarrow N$ be any smooth connected affine closed normal subgroup. The composite $S\hookrightarrow G$ is closed by composition of local quotient ring maps. To see normality, take a commutative $k$-algebra $B$, $g\in G(B)$ and $s\in S(B)$. Pulling back $m$ gives an fpqc covering on which $g=an$ with $a\in A$ and $n\in N$; this is a covering by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering, lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms]. Locally $gsg^{-1}=nsn^{-1}\in S$, because $a$ is central and $S$ is normal in $N$. These local lifts to $S$ agree on overlaps: their images in $G$ agree, and $S\hookrightarrow G$ is a monomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] they glue to an $S$-point, whose image equals $gsg^{-1}$ by uniqueness in the same lemma. Thus $S$ is normal in $G$, so it is trivial by the hypothesis on $G$. Induction applies to $N$ and proves that $N$ is proper.

source.place: Theorem 8.26, p.154, assertion that every affine connected normal subgroup of the almost-complement is normal in G; fpqc local multiplication makes the assertion valid on all algebra points.

proof.text: Both $A$ and $N$ are proper, so $A\times_kN$ is proper: its projection to $N$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and compose with $N\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-image-proper] to $m:A\times_kN\to G$, whose target is separated of finite type. Its scheme-theoretic image is proper over $k$. It is all of $G$: surjectivity of $m$ makes the image have all of $|G|$, and $G$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied over $k$. On any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $G$, the ideal $I$ of the image lies in every prime ideal since $V(I)=\operatorname{Spec}B$, hence in the nilradical, which is zero because $B$ is reduced. Thus the image ideal is zero. Hence $G$ is proper. The induction proves the required assertion for $G=Q$.

source.place: Theorem 8.26, p.154, last sentence of complete-central-component case; Appendix A.75(c),(d), p.583. Scheme-theoretic image: Stacks Tag 0AH6, morphisms.tex, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-is-proper.

Steps 1-6 follow the 8.26 route exactly: (1) induction set up on dim with the reduced central identity component A; (2) dim A=0 makes G affine, hence trivial; (3) A not proper would give a positive-dimensional affine U that is central and normal, a contradiction, so A is an abelian variety; (4) almost-complement N with dim N<d; (5) normality of S in G via an fpqc pullback of m, with descent along the monomorphism S→G; (6) the scheme-theoretic image of proper A×N under the surjective m is all of the reduced G, so G is proper. All three new nodes are true. Centre node: Milne 1.92 plus 8.11/8.1(a); no smoothness of Z assumed, which matters for SL_p in char p. Almost-complement node: 8.24 with the connected component of N_red; the dimension count gives surjectivity. Dichotomy node: 8.25 with the reduced identity component.
